The FCA reported that issues linked to third-party providers were the leading cause of operational incidents reported to the regulator between 2022 and 2023, a pattern the CrowdStrike Holdings outage brought into focus.

Following the CrowdStrike Holdings outage, the FCA told financial firms to increase operational resilience, giving them until March 2025 to prove they could maintain critical services during severe but plausible scenarios.
The CrowdStrike Holdings incident underscored the need for robust third-party IT risk management, a matter addressed by the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act which took effect in January 2025.
The CrowdStrike Holdings update failure disrupted banking, healthcare, retail and aviation, causing thousands of flight cancellations and widespread service degradation.
CrowdStrike Holdings released a defective Falcon content update for Microsoft Windows devices, causing a major outage. Around 8.5 million systems worldwide crashed as a result.

A US judge dismissed most of the SEC's accusations against SolarWinds Corporation and its CISO, finding that claims SolarWinds concealed security weaknesses after Sunburst rested on hindsight and speculation.
UBS is named among issuers on the SIX Group digital exchange platform, which reports more than CHF 2 billion issued through SIX Digital Exchange.
UBS names Chain IQ Group AG as its strategic sourcing partner, supporting sourcing and procurement activities including tendering. Chain IQ was spun off from UBS in 2013.
The LockBit ransomware group attacked Infosys McCamish Systems, a US-based subsidiary of Infosys providing services to insurance and financial clients.
SolarWinds Corporation faced investor pressure following the SEC fraud complaint, with the charges against both SolarWinds and a named executive raising governance concerns.

The SEC complaint against SolarWinds Corporation charged the company with fraud and internal and disclosure controls failures relating to known cybersecurity risks over a period from October 2018 until January 2021.

The SEC filed a complaint against SolarWinds Corporation and its chief information security officer Tim Brown, alleging they defrauded investors by overstating SolarWinds' cybersecurity practices and failing to disclose known risks.

The FCA penalty against Equifax Ltd highlighted the risk of outsourcing consumer data processing to a parent entity, arriving five years after the ICO had already fined Equifax for the same 2017 breach.
The UK Financial Conduct Authority fined Equifax Ltd GBP 11,164,400 for failing to manage and monitor the security of UK consumer data that Equifax had outsourced to its US parent.

The list of organisations breached through Progress Software's MOVEit kept climbing through 2023, demonstrating how one vulnerability in a widely embedded file-transfer product cascades through fourth-party relationships.

Ernst & Young, which provides certain services to Bank of America, was among the victims of the Progress Software MOVEit campaign. The breach at Ernst & Young exposed financial account information, credit card details and Social Security numbers of 30,210 Bank of America customers.
UBS executed its first cross-border intraday repo trade on the Broadridge Financial Solutions Distributed Ledger Repo platform, having onboarded to Broadridge DLR in 2021.
The Clop ransomware gang exploited a zero-day vulnerability in Progress Software's MOVEit Transfer platform, in a mass-exploitation campaign that affected hundreds of organisations worldwide.
Personal data relating to approximately 6.66 million individuals was exfiltrated from Capita plc, including special category data such as health and criminal record information.
Capita plc suffered a cyber incident that led to the exfiltration of personal data. Capita is a major outsourcing provider to UK public sector and financial services clients.
Post-incident analysis of the ION Group attack highlighted the systemic exposure created when many market participants depend on ION Group for the same critical function.
The ION Group ransomware attack disrupted trading, investment management and market analytics services that financial institutions and corporations rely on ION Group to provide.
Banks demanded answers from ION Group after the cyber attack, with the incident exposing how heavily derivatives markets depend on a single software provider.

Large customers of ION Group in the United States and Europe were forced to switch to manual processing of trades following the ransomware attack, causing significant delays across derivatives markets.
ION Group disclosed a ransomware incident affecting ION Cleared Derivatives, a division of ION Markets. The LockBit ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack on ION Group.
UBS announced an expansion of its cloud partnership with Microsoft Corporation, targeting more than 50% of its applications including critical workloads on Microsoft Azure within five years.

The rollout of the Broadridge Financial Solutions advisor workstation at UBS was publicly delayed. The UBS chief financial officer reaffirmed commitment to completing the Broadridge programme despite the delays.

Investigators established that attackers had been testing their ability to inject malicious code into SolarWinds Corporation builds as early as October 2019, more than a year before the Sunburst compromise was detected.
The Sunburst attack on SolarWinds Corporation was attributed to a Russian state-linked actor, with the trojanised Orion update distributed to SolarWinds customers including US federal agencies.

The Sunburst compromise of SolarWinds Corporation was a supply chain attack intended to reach SolarWinds' downstream customers, demonstrating how a single software vendor can propagate risk across thousands of organisations.
Threat actors gained access to SolarWinds Corporation's Orion software through its automated build environment, inserting the Sunburst backdoor that was distributed to SolarWinds customers.
SolarWinds Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC publicly disclosing the Sunburst supply chain attack, in which malicious code was inserted into its Orion network management software.

German financial regulator BaFin was criticised for its supervision of Wirecard AG, including its decision to pursue journalists and short sellers rather than investigate the allegations against Wirecard.
UBS cancelled its outsourcing partnership with Cognizant Technology Solutions, where reported spend had run up to around USD 330 million per year, as part of an insourcing strategy.
Scrutiny turned to EY's long-running audits of Wirecard AG, with critics arguing the auditor failed to uncover the fraud earlier. EY maintains that Wirecard concealed information from it.
Wirecard AG filed for insolvency, owing creditors approximately EUR 3.5 billion. Wirecard became the first DAX-listed company to collapse in this way.
Wirecard AG chief operating officer Jan Marsalek went into hiding to evade arrest and became the subject of an international manhunt.
Wirecard AG former chief executive Markus Braun was arrested by German authorities in connection with the Munich prosecutors' investigation.
Wirecard AG conceded that the EUR 1.9 billion in missing funds probably did not exist, an admission amounting to accounting fraud on its own balance sheet.
Wirecard AG shares collapsed after EY declined to sign the accounts, with the missing EUR 1.9 billion triggering a liquidity crisis at Wirecard.

EY refused to sign off Wirecard AG's 2019 financial statements. Wirecard disclosed that EUR 1.9 billion of company funds supposedly held in two Philippine banks was missing, and the banks disavowed ever holding it.
German police raided Wirecard AG offices after Munich prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into the Wirecard chief executive and three other management board members.
Cognizant Technology Solutions was hit by a Maze ransomware incident, raising security concerns among its financial services clients including UBS.
Wirecard AG shares fell sharply after the KPMG special audit failed to verify a majority of reported profits, with analysts questioning the reliability of Wirecard's accounts.
The KPMG special audit into Wirecard AG was published. KPMG said it was not able to verify the existence of the lion's share of the profits Wirecard reported between 2016 and 2018.
Under pressure from investors, Wirecard AG appointed KPMG to conduct a special audit of its financial reporting.
Under the settlement, Equifax Inc. allocated USD 300 million to consumer credit monitoring, USD 175 million to 48 states, and USD 100 million in civil penalties to the CFPB.
Equifax Inc. agreed to pay at least USD 575 million, and potentially up to USD 700 million, in a global settlement with the FTC, the CFPB and 50 US states and territories over the 2017 breach.
Broadridge Financial Solutions announced a wealth management technology agreement with UBS Americas, with UBS as anchor client for the Broadridge wealth platform.
The UK Information Commissioner's Office fined Equifax Ltd GBP 500,000, the maximum available under the pre-GDPR regime, over the 2017 breach affecting up to 15 million British citizens.
The DOJ and SEC announced charges against Sudhakar Reddy Bonthu, a former Equifax Inc. software development manager, for selling Equifax shares before the breach was publicly announced.

According to the SEC, the former Equifax Inc. executive realised proceeds of around USD 1 million and avoided more than USD 117,000 in losses by selling Equifax stock ahead of the breach announcement.
The SEC charged Jun Ying, a former Equifax Inc. executive next in line to be global chief information officer, with insider trading for selling Equifax shares before the breach was public.
Equifax Inc. faced sustained criticism over the delay between internal discovery of the breach in late July 2017 and public disclosure on 7 September.
Attackers moved through Equifax Inc. systems for 76 days before the intrusion was detected, and Equifax knew of the breach internally from late July before disclosing it in September.
Equifax Inc. publicly disclosed a data breach exposing the personal data of 147 million people, including Social Security numbers, birth dates and addresses.
Equifax Inc. administrators were instructed to apply a patch for a known Apache Struts vulnerability to affected systems. The patch was not applied, leaving Equifax exposed.

Cognizant Technology Solutions acquired the UBS India Service Centre in Hyderabad, with around 2,000 staff, and signed a multi-year services agreement covering BPO, IT and infrastructure management for UBS divisions globally.
